scope: Second attempt at the empty-tunnel alarm load: an object-chain continuity filter and a certified-path hazard rule
context: The first attempt (cross-section buckets of raw points) was rejected: it removed real detections and did not move the alarm load - results/empty-tunnel-alarm-load-20260919.json. The cause of its failure named the subject of this attempt: a bucket shares the wall behind a candidate with the candidate itself.

object_chain_continuity.idea: A duct, cable tray or walkway edge reaches one scan as a chain of small fragments at a single cross-section position, repeated along the whole scan; a fallen object is one cluster, or a few, at its own position. The chain is built from the candidate objects themselves, each placed by its OWN support, so nothing inherits a neighbouring structure's span.

hazard_requires_certified_path.idea: An object inside the *nominal* envelope where the path itself is not certified is a candidate, not a hazard: beyond the measured anchors the centre is extrapolated and on a drifting section is wrong by metres, so the tunnel's own surfaces appear to be inside the swept path. Such objects stay in the output with their distance and the reason `unsupported_nominal_envelope`.

hypothesis_for_the_close_range_class_dis.hypothesis: the walkway edge survives because in-gauge returns are protected from background removal (context keeps everything inside `observed & nominal_overlap`), so unprotecting them or letting the background model see them would remove the alarms at no cost

measured_on_frame_3_of_roundT_doubleT.background_model_verdict_on_those_points: 0 of 1101 explained by a fitted surface

hypothesis_for_the_close_range_class_dis.conclusion: the cheap fix does not exist: the protection rule touches 10 of 1101 points, and the background model already declines to call the walkway background. The walkway reaches the candidate stage because it is an in-scope structure that the fitted surfaces do not represent.
hypothesis_for_the_close_range_class_dis.what_this_leaves: the close-range boundary class needs a model of the tunnel's own structures - either fitted surfaces extended to the walkway and duct profiles, or an explicit per-route cross-section profile - and it must clear the gate already established: the labelled obstacle recording keeps every confirmed frame (52 of 52), inserted objects at 20/40/60 m keep reporting obstacle, and the targeted panel keeps event_recall 1.0 with empty scenes silent.

fourth_variant_rejected_status_level_dem.rule: hazards_require_inside_contour: only an object inside the reference contour is a hazard; boundary-ambiguous and uncertified-path objects stay in the output as candidates
fourth_variant_rejected_status_level_dem.what_it_fixed: the empty tunnel: roundT_doubleT went from 59 unresolved_obstacle frames to 60 of 60 no_obstacle_observed, and the labelled recording kept all 52 obstacle frames with its noise frames dropping 7 -> 1
fourth_variant_rejected_status_level_dem.what_it_broke: injected objects at 100 m: the object is still detected and still in the output (panel event_recall 1.0), but the frame status becomes no_obstacle_observed on every frame - the system reports a clear path while an object is present, at exactly the range the case scores as 'good'
fourth_variant_rejected_status_level_dem.why_it_is_wrong: status-level demotion trades false alarms for missed detections. The empty-tunnel false alarms must be removed at the OBJECT level - by not creating objects from the tunnel's own structures - not by softening what the frame status means.
fourth_variant_rejected_status_level_dem.verdict: rejected: it reported a clear path at 100 m while an object was there

fifth_variant_disproved_uncertainty_driv.hypothesis: the walkway is only 'possibly inside' because the bed-height uncertainty pushes the height band across the 13 cm contour step at 0.44 m, so tightening that uncertainty would clear the class with no semantic change
fifth_variant_disproved_uncertainty_driv.conclusion: the ambiguity is geometric, not an uncertainty artefact. The structure sits 4 cm outside the widest part of the contour against about 9 cm of combined knowledge, so any tightening that clears it would also clear a genuine object at the corridor edge. No further cheap avenue exists on the detection side.
fifth_variant_disproved_uncertainty_driv.what_remains: knowing that this structure is the walkway - the object-level tunnel-structure model - or the earlier two avenues: an external alignment, and the delivery path verified on a Docker host

sixth_attempt_tunnel_profile_model.research: the clearance-inspection and tunnel-modelling literature builds a track-relative frame (station, lateral, height), models the normal cross-section along the axis, and treats deviations from it as objects; the case's own hint is the same idea. Sources consulted: railway tunnel clearance inspection by mobile laser scanning (PMC5621173), rail-area extraction from references parallel to the rails (PMC11314673), Senstar/Blickfeld subway LiDAR deployment (marketing, no method), and the tunnel cross-section extraction line (IAARC, ISPRS, IOP)
sixth_attempt_tunnel_profile_model.implementation: one pass over the context cloud: group points by (lateral, height) cells of 0.4 m, count the DISTINCT station bins of 1 m inside each cell, and call a cell part of the tunnel's profile when it is occupied at >= 12 stations spanning >= 15 m. A candidate whose support lies mostly in profile cells is the tunnel, not an object. No temporal window, no map, no earlier pass.

results.far_class: unchanged: 699 confirmed hazards remain at median 122 m
results.frame_statuses: unchanged on both recordings - the wall is now driven only by the far class

sixth_attempt_tunnel_profile_model.why_the_far_class_survives: beyond the corridor horizon the lateral coordinate is our own extrapolation and is wrong by metres, so the tunnel's far surfaces drift across cells instead of forming a stable profile - the model is sound but the frame it works in is corrupted out there. Lowering the thresholds to 4 stations and a 10 m span changed nothing, which confirms the frame, not the threshold, is the limit.
sixth_attempt_tunnel_profile_model.verdict: reverted: it is the right mechanism and it removes the infrastructure classes without touching a single real detection, but it costs 14 percent and changes no frame decision, because the remaining driver is the far class that needs a trustworthy lateral frame first
sixth_attempt_tunnel_profile_model.what_this_leaves: the empty-tunnel wall is now attributable to exactly one class - the tunnel's own surfaces at 90-164 m, placed by an extrapolated centre. Fixing that needs the far-field lateral frame (external alignment, or a centre estimated from something that survives at range), and then this profile model removes the rest.

seventh_avenue_researched_and_disproved.problem: the far-field lateral frame: the last class (the tunnel's own surfaces at 90-164 m) is placed by an extrapolated centre

how_the_field_solves_it.map_based_localization: Daoust & Barfoot, 'Infrastructure-Free Mapping and Localization for Tunnel-Based Rail Applications Using 2D Lidar' (UTIAS, 2017; MASC thesis, and the IEEE IV 2016 paper): sliding-window RQE scan matching with WALL REMOVAL, mapping and localizing relative to a map. Needs a prior map of the route; the organizers' bags are unseen single passes.
how_the_field_solves_it.cross_section_fitting: the clearance-inspection line (railway tunnel clearance by mobile laser scanning, PMC5621173; tunnel cross-section extraction, IAARC/ISPRS/IOP; Taubin ellipse and least-squares circle fitting for lining analysis) fits the tunnel cross-section and uses its axis as the lateral reference, per station rather than as a carried constant.
how_the_field_solves_it.profile_models: modelling the normal cross-section along the axis and calling deviations objects (attempt six, works only where the frame is trustworthy)

premise_tested_on_our_data.method: Taubin circle fit in the cross-section plane to raw returns within a 2 m slab at 40/80/120/160 m, centres compared with the rail-derived centre at 20 m, over six consecutive frames
premise_tested_on_our_data.conclusion: the radius is well determined but the centre is not: a partial, sparse arc leaves its centre ill-conditioned along the arc, and beyond 80 m there are too few returns to fit at all. The field's per-station fit cannot give a trustworthy lateral frame at range on this sensor.

seventh_avenue_researched_and_disproved.verdict: avenue closed by measurement, not by opinion. The far-field lateral frame is not obtainable in a single pass from this sensor by cross-section fitting, and map-based localization needs a prior map of the route.
seventh_avenue_researched_and_disproved.what_this_completes: fifth independent measurement of the same limit: rails vanish by 90 m, the bed band is empty beyond 70 m, a carried bore offset is biased about 1 m, six estimators failed, and now partial-arc circle fits are ill-conditioned and unmeasurable beyond 80 m. The far-field lateral frame is a sensor property on this route, not a modelling gap.

eighth_attempt_geometric_feature_classif.research: the field separates a tunnel's own structures from its content by local geometric feature classification: the eigenvalues of the local covariance give planar (lining, wall, duct), linear (cable, rail) or compact (object) evidence, with the normal giving the surface orientation. Sources: ISPRS 2015 robust planar and linear feature classification, ISPRS 2020 planar polygon detection, ISPRS 2021 detection of railway-related infrastructures, semantic segmentation of tunnel ground/lining/wiring/rails (ISPRS 2020), tunnel secondary lining segmentation by roughness and features.
eighth_attempt_geometric_feature_classif.implementation: eigen-decomposition of the covariance of each track's ACCUMULATED, ego-motion compensated support - which needs several observations and never a good lateral frame - scoped to candidates that do not intersect the certified corridor, so a planar object genuinely on the path stays a hazard

measured.objects_reclassified: 128 at planarity <= 0.08, with no change to any frame status
measured.threshold_sweep: 0.15 and 0.30 both leave the statuses unchanged on both recordings, with the labelled obstacle preserved 52 of 52
measured.remaining_after: 980 confirmed hazards of which 856 carry at least the 8 accumulated voxels the test needs, so the blocker is the planarity criterion, not the point floor
measured.cost: within noise (132 vs 134 ms, 145 vs 147 ms)

eighth_attempt_geometric_feature_classif.why_it_fails: the accumulated world-frame evidence of those far structures is not planar: with a handful of returns per scan and imperfect registration it is smeared, so the shape test sees no surface. The test is sound; the evidence it must judge is degraded.
eighth_attempt_geometric_feature_classif.verdict: reverted: no frame decision changed, so nothing ships
eighth_attempt_geometric_feature_classif.cumulative_statement: six independent approaches have now failed to separate the tunnel's far-field surfaces from objects within a single pass on this sensor: the lateral frame (five separate measurements), the track-relative profile model, per-station circle fitting, sparse candidate admission, and now shape-based feature classification. The far returns are too few and the registration too imperfect for geometry to decide. The remaining options are structural, not algorithmic: a prior map from another pass, or an explicit decision about what an unclassifiable far return should mean in the output contract.
